correctness.rationale: For every integer \(H\ge2\), the exact domain is the integral companion map \(A_{t,d}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-d\\1&t\end{pmatrix}\) with \(|t|,|d|\le H\) and both eigenvalues strictly outside the unit circle. The quadratic Schur test gives precisely \(E(H)=2H^2-2\). The geometric iff criterion is a cited source theorem (Hughes--de Jong, Theorem 1.2). The spectral argument classifies distinct integer roots and nonrational conjugate roots: power integrality forces a root-of-unity quotient, and rational algebraic-integrality of \(2\cos(2\theta)\) restricts \(t^2/d\) to \(0,1,2,3,4\); the repeated-root case is excluded because the companion minimal polynomial has degree two. Exact power identities prove each converse. Signed integer-root pairs are counted through \(Q(H)=D(H)-2H+1\); correcting their Jordan diagonal, the trace-zero overlap, and the three quadratic nonreal families yields the asserted \(N(H)=2D(H)-2H+2\lfloor\sqrt{H/2}\rfloor+2\lfloor\sqrt{H/3}\rfloor\). Dirichlet hyperbola proves the linear secondary term and density. Boundary cases, trace cutoff and all family overlaps were reconstructed; exact-integer matrix-power discriminant checks independently match all 64 integer height boxes from \(H=2\) through \(H=65\). Finite calculations are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The principal geometric iff theorem and finite exponent-list in dimension two belong to HDJ (2026), and the Dirichlet divisor asymptotic is classical. The newly assessed claim is an exact all-height census of canonical companion maps and its two-term relative frequency. Full accessible primary HTML sections of HDJ, especially Theorem 1.2 and Section 5.2, were read and do not present this count, and targeted semantic plus web queries found no direct covering enumeration. Earlier Cawley work is restricted to automorphisms of unit determinant and hence does not imply a height count for expanding degree>=2 companions. A previous four-dimensional spectral-exponent classification concerns a different parameter/invariant and gives no 2D height counts. Search failure is not asserted to be a proof of priority; a potential earlier equivalent arithmetic count is a residual risk.
residual_risks: The historical completeness of synonym-based literature searches is limited; a prior divisor-sum count under algebraic-number terminology may exist.

value.rationale: The source frames nonsmoothness as an “almost always” phenomenon without a quantitative arithmetic abundance measure. Bounding the trace and determinant of 2-by-2 companions is a natural conjugacy-invariant height model with exactly 2H^2-2 expanding representatives. The new all-H count discovers precise arithmetic cancellation among repeated Jordan spectra, trace-zero maps, and the three possible complex root-of-unity families; it quantifies their frequency with an exact logarithmic coefficient and an explicit linear second term. Thus it supplies both a computable cutoff census for any H and an asymptotic statement of how rare smooth boundaries are in this canonical expanding family, not an arbitrary small parameter slice. It does not claim a general entry-height matrix census or optimal partition cardinalities.
